_comment: The turn-SEVERITY rule, as a table both languages must satisfy.
A severity is HOW BADLY a turn ended, derived from its outcome and from nothing
else. It exists because five surfaces each carried their own partial answer to
that one question and disagreed: the transcript divider, the collapsed face and
the footer glyph all read `interrupted` as a failure, while the tab dot and the
favicon cue read it as nothing at all — so a network error that stopped a turn
showed an inline error message beside a hollow 'nothing is happening here' ring.
The rule is implemented twice for TurnOutcome's own reason (internal/vibekit's
SeverityOf for the server's surfaces, static-src/turn-severity.ts for the
client's five), so this file is the contract between them. It is read by Go's
TestTurnSeverityContract (internal/vibekit/turns_test.go) and by
static-src/turn-severity.node.test.ts. Change the rule in one language and the
other language's test fails.
It lives beside SeverityOf rather than beside turn_outcomes.json, which pins a
rule internal/chat implements: a fixture belongs with the function it pins, so
neither test has to reach into another package's testdata.
`default_reason` is in the same table rather than a second one because it is
the same kind of fact and drifts the same way: the client needs it as the
fallback for every turn persisted before turn_failure_reason existed, and two
hand-written copies of one sentence is exactly what a shared fixture prevents.
It is keyed per OUTCOME rather than per severity, because a reader wants the
distinction the severity throws away — a refusal and a dropped connection are
both broken and want different words. Empty means there is nothing to say.
COVERAGE IS ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: every row must match, and the rows
must cover every TurnOutcome constant. An eighth outcome therefore fails this
test rather than sliding through to a surface with no case for it.

cases._why: In flight. No settled mark on any surface, and nothing to explain.
The absence of a mark IS the clean case; a mark on every row says nothing.
The user asked for it, so it must not read alarming — and it produced no answer, so it must not read clean either.

cases.default_reason: The turn was interrupted before the agent finished.
cases._why: A fault nobody chose. THIS ROW is the fix for the hollow tab dot: four surfaces already called it a failure and the dot's latch was the one that did not.

cases.default_reason: The agent reported an error and the turn stopped.

cases._why: Nothing malfunctioned, but the turn produced no answer and the remedy is a different prompt or model — which is a thing to act on, so it is broken rather than stopped.

cases.default_reason: The turn ended for a reason vibekit could not read.
cases._why: ConcludeStopReason's ruling holds: an unmeasured stop reason says nothing about whether the work succeeded, so grading it broken would report a working turn as failed. Equally not clean — a status mark may fall back to ambiguous, never to reassuring.
